title: Cloud Connector on AWS: VM size, EC2 instance type, and matching the provisioning template

prose.text: Two choices must agree: the VM size in the provisioning template and the EC2 instance type the template or module launches.

prose.label: Size must match the template.
prose.text: {{size-must-match}} {{module-size-variable}} Autoscaling takes only the small size: [[cloud-connector.aws.autoscaling]].

prose.label: What the reference Terraform module accepts.
prose.text: {{module-instance-types}} The module's list is wider than the guide's {{divergence:small-instance-list}}. {{module-size-pairing}} {{mismatch-applies-cleanly}}

prose.label: Interfaces.
prose.text: The number of network interfaces follows the size: [[cloud-connector.aws.interfaces]].

checks.do: Whether the VM size in the provisioning template equals the instance size given to the CloudFormation template or Terraform module.
Whether the EC2 instance type is one the deployment guide lists for that size, and not an M5 or C5 type such as m5.large or c5.large.
After a Terraform apply that created no Cloud Connector, whether errorlog.txt in the root module directory reports invalid parameters.

vm-sizes.statement: The AWS deployment guide lists Small VMs on m5n.large, c5a.large, m6i.large (recommended) or c6i.large, and Medium and Large VMs, both deprecated, on m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge (recommended) or c6i.4xlarge.

quotes: Small VM: Requires one of the following Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances: m5n.large, c5a.large, m6i.large (recommended), or c6i.large.
Medium VM (deprecated): Requires one of the following EC2 instances: m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge (recommended), or c6i.4xlarge.
Large VM (deprecated): Requires one of the following EC2 instances: m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge (recommended), or c6i.4xlarge.

small-recommended.statement: Zscaler recommends the Small VM size in the provisioning template and the m6i instance for best performance and security, with the latest available AMI.

quotes: Zscaler recommends selecting the VM Size as Small.
For the best performance and security, always deploy the latest available AMI and the recommended m6i instance.

m5-c5-retired.statement: The EC2 M5 and C5 instance families are no longer available from the AWS Marketplace or Zscaler deployment templates, and existing Cloud Connectors on them (such as m5.large or c5.large) should be redeployed on a supported instance.

quotes: The Amazon EC2 M5 and C5 instance families are no longer available from the AWS Marketplace or Zscaler deployment templates.
If you have any existing Cloud Connector deployments based on M5 or C5 instances (such as m5.large or c5.large), redeploy and migrate them to one of the supported instances listed above.

marketplace-validated.statement: AWS Marketplace restricts Cloud Connector to instances Zscaler validated, a list Zscaler reviews periodically, and Zscaler cannot guarantee that VMs on unsupported instances function properly.

quotes: AWS Marketplace restricts instances to those that Zscaler validated. Zscaler periodically reviews and updates this list.
Zscaler cannot guarantee that VMs deployed on unsupported instances will function properly.

size-must-match.statement: The instance size given to the deployment (small, medium or large) must match the VM size of the cloud provisioning template; if the provisioning URL's sizing and the deployment template's sizing differ, the deployment is unsuccessful.

quotes: Your Cloud Connector instance size selection of small, medium (deprecated), or large (deprecated) must match the selected VM size of the configured cloud provisioning template.
If the sizing demonstrated in the cloud provisioning URL and the deployment template do not match, Cloud Connector deployment is unsuccessful.

module-size-variable.statement: The reference CCVM module's `cc_instance_size` accepts small, medium or large, defaults to small, and is described as determined by and needing to match the provisioning template.

quotes: Cloud Connector Instance size. Determined by and needs to match the Cloud Connector Portal provisioning template configuration
default = "small"
var.cc_instance_size == "small" || var.cc_instance_size == "medium" || var.cc_instance_size == "large"

module-instance-types.statement: The reference CCVM module defaults `ccvm_instance_type` to m6i.large and its validation accepts only t3.medium, m5n.large, c5a.large, m6i.large, c6i.large, c6in.large, m7i.large, m7i-flex.large, m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge, c6i.4xlarge and c6in.4xlarge.

quotes: default     = "m6i.large"

var.ccvm_instance_type == "t3.medium" || var.ccvm_instance_type == "m5n.large" || var.ccvm_instance_type == "c5a.large" || var.ccvm_instance_type == "m6i.large" || var.ccvm_instance_type == "c6i.large" ||
var.ccvm_instance_type == "c6in.large" || var.ccvm_instance_type == "m7i.large" || var.ccvm_instance_type == "m7i-flex.large" || var.ccvm_instance_type == "m5n.4xlarge"
var.ccvm_instance_type == "m6i.4xlarge" || var.ccvm_instance_type == "c6i.4xlarge" || var.ccvm_instance_type == "c6in.4xlarge"
Input ccvm_instance_type must be set to an approved vm instance type.

module-size-pairing.statement: The CCVM module pairs medium and large only with m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge, c6i.4xlarge or c6in.4xlarge; when size and type do not pair, it creates no Cloud Connector instance and a local-exec appends a message beginning "Cloud Connector parameters were invalid. No appliances were created." and naming cc_instance_size and ccvm_instance_type to errorlog.txt in the root module directory.

quotes: medium_cc_instance = ["m5n.4xlarge", "m6i.4xlarge", "c6i.4xlarge", "c6in.4xlarge"]
large_cc_instance = ["m5n.4xlarge", "m6i.4xlarge", "c6i.4xlarge", "c6in.4xlarge"]
contains(local.medium_cc_instance, var.ccvm_instance_type) && var.cc_instance_size == "medium"
count = local.valid_cc_create ? 0 : 1 # 0 means no error is thrown, else throw error

echo "Cloud Connector parameters were invalid. No appliances were created. Please check the documentation and cc_instance_size / ccvm_instance_type values that were chosen" >> ${path.root}/errorlog.txt
count = local.valid_cc_create ? var.cc_count : 0

mismatch-applies-cleanly.statement: A size and type mismatch therefore surfaces as an apply that creates zero Cloud Connectors and a line in errorlog.txt, not as a validation error at plan time.
mismatch-applies-cleanly.conditions: Follows from the pairing check being a count on the resources plus an echo in a null_resource provisioner rather than a variable validation; Terraform semantics, not stated by the module.

cfn-instance-types.statement: The CloudFormation templates default the EC2 instance type to m6i.large and accept t3.medium, c5a.large, m5n.large, m6i.large, c6i.large, c6in.large, m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge, c6i.4xlarge and c6in.4xlarge; template rules require one of m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge, c6i.4xlarge and c6in.4xlarge for the medium and large sizes.

quotes: AllowedValues: - t3.medium - c5a.large - m5n.large - m6i.large - c6i.large - c6in.large - m5n.4xlarge - m6i.4xlarge - c6i.4xlarge - c6in.4xlarge Default: m6i.large
For medium CCInstanceType, the Instance type must be one of m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge, c6i.4xlarge, c6in.4xlarge
largeCCInstanceType: RuleCondition: !Equals - !Ref CCInstanceType - large Assertions: - Assert: 'Fn::Contains': - - m5n.4xlarge - m6i.4xlarge - c6i.4xlarge - c6in.4xlarge
Default: "m6i.large" AllowedValues: - t3.medium - c5a.large - m5n.large - m6i.large - c6i.large - c6in.large - m5n.4xlarge - m6i.4xlarge - c6i.4xlarge - c6in.4xlarge

cfn-instance-history.statement: The changelog records that version 1.0.0 made m6i.large the default for small and m6i.4xlarge for medium and large, added the m5n, m6i and c6i families and removed the m5 family, 1.3.1 added c6in, and 1.3.2 removed t3a.medium and c4.4xlarge.

quotes: - new default/recommend EC2 type for small CCs: m6i.large; medium/large: m6i.4xlarge - add: m5n, m6i, and c6i family support - remove: m5 family support
* feat: add c6in family as supported EC2 instance type
* refactor: CC VM EC2 instance type constraint cleanup (removal of t3a.medium and c4.4xlarge)

small-instance-list.summary: Which EC2 types a Small Cloud Connector may use: the deployment guide lists four, the reference Terraform module accepts twelve and the CloudFormation templates ten.

positions.says: Small VMs require m5n.large, c5a.large, m6i.large or c6i.large.

quotes: Small VM: Requires one of the following Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances: m5n.large, c5a.large, m6i.large (recommended), or c6i.large.

positions.says: The small size also accepts t3.medium, c6in.large, m7i.large, m7i-flex.large and the 4xlarge types m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge, c6i.4xlarge and c6in.4xlarge.

quotes: small_cc_instance  = ["t3.medium", "m5n.large", "c5a.large", "m6i.large", "c6i.large", "c6in.large", "m7i.large", "m7i-flex.large", "m5n.4xlarge", "m6i.4xlarge", "c6i.4xlarge", "c6in.4xlarge"]

positions.says: The CloudFormation templates accept ten types, including t3.medium and c6in.large but not the m7i types.

quotes: AllowedValues: - t3.medium - c5a.large - m5n.large - m6i.large - c6i.large - c6in.large - m5n.4xlarge - m6i.4xlarge - c6i.4xlarge - c6in.4xlarge Default: m6i.large
For medium CCInstanceType, the Instance type must be one of m5n.4xlarge, m6i.4xlarge, c6i.4xlarge, c6in.4xlarge

small-instance-list.impact: A module deployment can pass validation on a type the guide does not list (t3.medium, c6in.large, the m7i types), and the guide says Zscaler cannot guarantee unsupported instances work.
